mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three consecutive months in at least 80% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months in at least 70% of out-of-sample episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a broad-based demand collapse, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% for three months signals a disinflationary tightening regime that raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods of rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 mean excess return) during periods when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, coupled with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates elevated precautionary savings and muted consumption growth, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for 6 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (|UNRATE - 12-month MA| < 0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months and UNRATE is stable.
